key_decisions.rationale: Keeps precise day, event, place, and maternal presence.

key_decisions.after: On the third day there was a wedding in Cana of Galilee, and Jesus’ mother was there.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains respectful but distancing address, difficult idiom, and hour theme.

key_decisions.after: Jesus said to her, “Woman, what does this have to do with you and me? My hour has not yet come.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And Jesus says to her, “What to me and to you, woman? My hour has not yet come.”

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps exact number, stone, ritual use, and ancient capacity.

key_decisions.after: Six stone water jars were standing there for Jewish purification, each holding two or three measures.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Now there were six stone water jars set there for the purification of the Jews, each holding two or three measures.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves transformation, unequal knowledge, servants’ witness, and groom.
key_decisions.before: When the master of the banquet tasted the water that had become wine, he did not know where it came from, though the servants who drew the water knew. He called the bridegroom
key_decisions.after: When the banquet master tasted the water that had become wine, he did not know where it came from, though the servants who had drawn the water knew. He called the bridegroom
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And when the master of the feast tasted the water having become wine and did not know where it came from (but the servants who had drawn the water knew), the master of the feast calls the bridegroom

key_decisions.rationale: Retains social custom, intoxication reference, quality contrast, and surprise.
key_decisions.before: and said, “Everyone serves the good wine first, and when people have drunk freely, the inferior wine. You have kept the good wine until now.”
key_decisions.after: and said, “Everyone serves the good wine first and then the inferior wine after people have drunk freely. But you have kept the good wine until now.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: and says to him, “Every person sets out the good wine first, and when they have drunk freely, then the inferior; you have kept the good wine until now.”

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps first sign, place, glory revelation, and disciple belief.
key_decisions.before: Jesus did this beginning of signs in Cana of Galilee and revealed his glory, and his disciples trusted in him.
key_decisions.after: Jesus did this in Cana of Galilee as the beginning of his signs. He revealed his glory, and his disciples believed in him.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: This beginning of signs Jesus did in Cana of Galilee and manifested his glory, and his disciples believed in him.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps festival designation, nearness, and ascent.
key_decisions.before: The Jewish Passover was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
key_decisions.after: The Jewish Passover was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And the Passover of the Jews was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

key_decisions.rationale: Names all animals, sellers, changers, and sacred setting.
key_decisions.before: In the temple he found people selling cattle, sheep, and doves, and money changers sitting at their tables.
key_decisions.after: In the temple courts he found people selling cattle, sheep, and doves, and the money changers seated at their tables.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And he found in the temple those selling oxen and sheep and doves, and the money changers sitting.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves improvised whip, expulsion, animals, coins, and overturned tables without saying he struck people.
key_decisions.before: He made a whip from cords and drove them all out of the temple, along with the sheep and cattle. He poured out the money changers’ coins and overturned their tables.
key_decisions.after: He made a whip from cords and drove them all out of the temple courts, including the sheep and cattle. He poured out the money changers’ coins and overturned their tables.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And making a whip of cords, he drove them all out of the temple, both the sheep and the oxen, and poured out the coins of the money changers and overturned the tables,

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps dove sellers, commands, Father’s house, and commerce critique.
key_decisions.before: He told those selling doves, “Take these things out of here! Stop making my Father’s house a house of trade.”
key_decisions.after: He told those selling doves, “Take these things away from here! Stop making my Father’s house a marketplace!”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: and to those selling the doves he said, “Take these things away from here; do not make my Father’s house a house of trade.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves later remembering and scriptural line.

key_decisions.after: His disciples remembered that it is written, “Zeal for your house will consume me.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: His disciples remembered that it is written, “Zeal for your house will consume me.”

key_decisions.rationale: Clarifies institutional challenge while retaining sign and authorization.
key_decisions.before: The Jewish leaders responded, “What sign can you show us to justify doing these things?”
key_decisions.after: The Jewish authorities responded, “What sign can you show us to authorize your doing these things?”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Therefore the Jews answered and said to him, “What sign do you show us, since you are doing these things?”

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps imperative, inner sanctuary term, exact days, and raising.

key_decisions.after: Jesus answered them, “Destroy this sanctuary, and in three days I will raise it.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Jesus answered and said to them, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves exact years, contrast, and incredulous question.
key_decisions.before: The leaders said, “This temple has been under construction for forty-six years, and you will raise it in three days?”
key_decisions.after: The authorities replied, “This sanctuary has been under construction for forty-six years, and you will raise it in three days?”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Then the Jews said, “This temple was built in forty-six years, and will you raise it in three days?”

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps narrator’s bodily interpretation and sanctuary metaphor.

key_decisions.after: But he was speaking about the sanctuary of his body.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But he was speaking about the temple of his body.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves resurrection, remembering, and dual belief.

key_decisions.after: So when he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and they believed the Scripture and the word Jesus had spoken.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Therefore when he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and they believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken.

key_decisions.after: While Jesus was in Jerusalem during the Passover Festival, many believed in his name when they saw the signs he was doing.
